newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares off to rocky start on EMU, Bonn woes.
newsitem.headline: German shares off to rocky start on EMU, Bonn woes.

text.p: German shares got off to a rocky start in bourse trade on Tuesday, falling slightly in volatile trade due to worries about the single European currency and the future of the ruling Bonn coalition.
The 30-share DAX index fell 18.98 points at 3,648.45 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer trade, was down 19.72 points at 3,648.89 points.
"I do not expect more losses at the moment but some uneven trading as the market decides what to do next," said one Stuttgart-based trader after Monday's steep drop.
Little corporate news was expected during the session and many traders were on the sidelines as the market suffered at the outset from relatively weak volumes.

Instead, market attention remained focused on worries about currency union after new French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said he wanted to delay an agreement on the stability pact designed to ensure budgetary discipline under monetary union, triggering worries the project will be delayed.
Some market participants said the market had overreacted to Strauss-Kahn's remarks and that the dollar remaining above 1.71 marks and overnight Wall Street gains would support the market.
"It's a good sign that the market is remaining stable despite the low volumes," said a Frankfurt share trader.
Among specific shares, dollar-sensitive shares that took the brunt of selling on Monday's afternoon slide started to recover in early Tuesday dealings.
Chemical group Hoechst AG rose 10 pfennigs to 69.90 marks, while carmakers Volkswagen AG rose three marks to 1,189 marks and BMW AG was up six marks at 1,372 marks.
